sections.h2: Paperwork for a Texas sale without an agent
sections.html:
A Texas owner selling without an agent still has to hand the buyer a Seller's Disclosure Notice, use a written contract, and record a signed and acknowledged deed with the county clerk. No agent is needed for any of those steps, but each one has rules attached.

The Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) publishes the disclosure as Form 55-1 for sellers of previously occupied single family homes, and it applies to contracts entered into on or after September 1, 2023. It covers the material facts and physical condition of the property that Section 5.008 of the Property Code calls for.

  • Seller's Disclosure Notice (TREC 55-1) for a previously occupied single-family home
  • A federal lead-based paint disclosure if the house was built before 1978
  • A groundwater and surface water rights disclosure when the contract calls for it
  • Notice to Prospective Buyer (TREC 58-0), which covers title advice and utility district notices
  • A deed that is signed and acknowledged, then recorded in the land's home county

The TREC form page carries the current version. The Property Code lists situations where the notice is not required, so ask a Texas real estate attorney if you are unsure whether your sale qualifies.

Some disclosures come from state law, some from the standard TREC contract, and one from federal law. Which ones you need depends on the house and the contract.

Common disclosures for a Texas for-sale-by-owner house
DisclosureWhen it appliesPublished by
Seller's Disclosure Notice, Form 55-1Previously occupied single family residence, under Property Code Sec. 5.008TREC
Seller's Disclosure About Groundwater and Surface Water RightsDefault under TREC contracts unless every statement in Paragraph 7I(3) is trueTREC
Notice to Prospective Buyer, Form 58-0Abstract or title policy advice, and utility district noticesTREC
Lead-based paint disclosure and pamphletMost housing built before 1978U.S. EPA

The water disclosure is the one that surprises sellers. No other law requires it, so it comes up only when the parties use a TREC contract, and an exemption from the Seller's Disclosure Notice does not automatically excuse it. A well, pond, lake or water tank on the lot, or any known severed or leased groundwater right, can make the form necessary.

Surface water rights mean a permit, certified filing or certificate of adjudication from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality that allows diversion, impoundment or use of surface water. If you do not know whether your tract has one, ask an attorney.

sections.h2: Federal rules for a house built before 1978
sections.html:
The EPA's Lead-based Paint Disclosure Rule covers most private housing built before 1978, and it puts the burden on the seller whether or not an agent is involved. Foreclosure sales, zero-bedroom units, housing built after 1977, and housing tested and found free of lead-based paint by a certified inspector fall outside it.

  • Give the buyer the EPA pamphlet, Protect Your Family From Lead In Your Home.
  • Disclose what you know about lead-based paint and lead hazards, and hand over any records or reports.
  • Include a Lead Warning Statement in or attached to the contract, with confirmation that you complied.
  • Offer a 10-day window for a paint inspection or risk assessment, which the buyer may waive or the parties may change in writing.
  • Keep the signed disclosure for three years after the sale closes.

EPA publishes sample seller's disclosure forms in English and Spanish. Penalties are possible for a seller who skips the rule, so an owner of an older Texas house should handle this before accepting an offer, not after.

sections.h2: Do I need a license to sell my own house in Texas?
sections.html:
A license is not required for an individual employed by a property owner to buy or sell real property on the owner's behalf (Rule 535.5(c)). For a sale of your own house, call TREC to confirm before relying on that answer.

The point matters most when title sits in an LLC or corporation and a family member or employee is handling the sale. It does not cover selling a property you do not own or taking a fee to market someone else's house. If the facts are unclear, a short call to a Texas real estate attorney costs less than a licensing complaint.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and clearing title
sections.html:
A deed gets filed with the clerk of the county that holds the land. It must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer such as a notary, or witnessed by two subscribing witnesses. General warranty, special warranty, quitclaim, trustee's and sheriff's deeds are all filed there.

Recording fees are set locally. Dallas, Denton and Ellis counties each print a $25 first-page charge and $4 for later pages, with differences in add-ons. Ask the county clerk for the current fee page and any rules on return addresses, ID and payment, since those vary by county.

  • Title search. A title company or lawyer checks recorded liens, judgments and the chain of owners before closing.
  • Payoff and release. A mortgage balance is paid at closing and the lender records a release of lien.
  • Inherited houses. No law forces third parties to accept an affidavit of heirship, so a muniment of title, executor's deed or transfer on death deed may be needed instead.
  • Contracts for deed. Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D covers executory contracts for residential property, and the purchaser has a statutory right to cancel.

sections.h2: Property taxes and exemptions in the year of sale
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1, and the owner on that day is liable for the year. The contract has to say who pays what for the year of sale. Appraisal districts value property as of January 1, bills go out around October 1, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1 with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

A buyer who takes title after January 1 can claim a homestead exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not receive it. School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and owners 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 school exemption. Bring tax receipts, exemption letters and any over-65 ceiling paperwork to closing so the title company can prorate correctly.

Texas also caps annual increases in appraised value for a residence homestead at 10 percent.

A Texas homeowner facing non-judicial foreclosure works on a short, fixed timeline, and selling before the auction is one way out. After a notice of default, the borrower may cure by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of receiving it. The servicer must then send a Notice of Sale at least 21 days before the sale.

Auctions are public and run between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month, or the first Wednesday if the first Tuesday is January 1 or July 4. If you are in this position, call the servicer, find the sale date on the posted notice, and have a title company confirm the payoff before you list at a price the market will bear.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
A for-sale-by-owner file goes faster when the paper is ready on the first day a buyer asks.

  • The deed you took title under, so the legal description and owner names can be copied exactly.
  • A current payoff letter if a lender holds a lien.
  • Your most recent tax bill and any exemption letters.
  • Records of repairs and permits, which help you fill in the disclosure notice honestly.
  • Well, pond or water tank details if the lot has any.

With these in hand you can fill in the Seller's Disclosure Notice, ask a title company to open an order, and tell the buyer what to expect at closing: the deed is signed before a notary, the lender is paid off, and the clerk records the deed.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a Seller's Disclosure Notice if I sell my Texas house myself?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Form 55-1 is required of sellers of previously occupied single family residences under Property Code Sec. 5.008. Having no agent does not remove the duty, though the statute lists situations where the notice does not apply.

faqs.q: Is the groundwater and surface water disclosure required by Texas law?
faqs.a: No other law requires it. It becomes part of the deal when the parties use a TREC contract, unless every statement in Paragraph 7I(3) of the One to Four Family Residential Contract is true.

It is the Notice to Prospective Buyer. The buyer acknowledges being advised to have an attorney examine the abstract or to buy a title insurance policy, and the form carries statutory notices that matter if the property lies in a utility district.

faqs.q: Does a federal lead paint disclosure apply to my Texas home?
faqs.a: Only if the house was built before 1978. For most private housing from that era, the EPA rule requires the pamphlet, a disclosure of what you know, a Lead Warning Statement and a 10-day inspection window for the buyer.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a for-sale-by-owner closing in Texas?
faqs.a: At the office of the clerk for the county that holds the house. The deed must be acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer, or witnessed by two subscribing witnesses, and the county sets its own fee and filing rules.
